Subject: Private deployment: Helios networking requirements and questions

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks for the intro last week. We are preparing an internal approval packet for a Redwood Private deployment (HIPAA-bound workloads) and I'd like actionable guidance on the networking approach. High-level constraints:

- We run production workloads across two AWS accounts (us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 DR).
- Strict PHI controls: no shared routing across unrelated accounts without an audited boundary.
- Need predictable low latency for synchronous inference (<30ms p95 target within our region).
- Egress IP stability required for allowlisting with our security appliance.
- We may have an on-prem DR site that needs intermittent access.

Attached is our current network diagram and a SOC2 questionnaire that your security team started filling out (helios-network-diagram-v1.pdf; redwood-soc2-questions.xlsx).

Specific ask: can you summarize tradeoffs between VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and a site-to-site VPN for this deployment, and recommend a primary approach + fallback? Also please outline any procurement/networking items we should add to the MSA/SoW (e.g., static egress IPs, audit logs retention, required ENI placements).

Can we set up a technical 30-min call? Greg (procurement) may join for procurement items. Proposed window: Tue 11/3 10-12 PT.

Thanks,
Anna

Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. We're happy to help. I'll put a concise summary below and follow up with a short tech note from Karthik that goes deeper.

Quick executive summary (short):
- Recommended primary: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) into a dedicated Redwood-managed VPC endpoint service.
  - Why: preserves account-level isolation (ENIs in your VPC), supports allowlisting of Helios egress IPs by using dedicated NAT or proxy in your subnets, and is strongly aligned with HIPAA boundary requirements since traffic never traverses public internet.
- Fallback / secondary: Site-to-site VPN for on-prem DR and as a backup path between accounts (encrypted, configurable HA).
- VPC peering: viable only if both Helios accounts host the Redwood stack (same account or explicit peering), but peering shares a route table relationship which complicates strict tenant boundaries and audit isolation — generally not our first choice for cross-account multi-tenant SaaS patterns.

Procurement / contract items to consider (short list):
- Static egress IP guarantees for PrivateLink — required for allowlisting.
- Endpoint SLA (latency target, availability) and metrics exposure via Redwood Console.
- Audit log retention duration and delivery (CloudTrail + VPC Flow logs to S3 / SIEM).
- Change control for endpoint IPs/ENIs and notification windows for maintenance.

I'll loop Karthik for a technical tradeoff table and a brief draft of the mutual action plan. If Tue 11/3 10am PT works, I'll send a calendar invite and include Greg.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Anna / team — adding a technical comparison and concrete configuration notes below. Long version for your architecture review.

1) VPC Peering- Pros:
  - Low latency (single-digit ms intra-region) because traffic stays on AWS backbone.
  - Simple to set up for same-account or tightly-controlled cross-account peering.
  - No extra proxies or NAT required if IP ranges don't overlap.
- Cons:
  - Transitive routing is not supported; would need manual route management across multiple peering relationships for multi-account or multi-region.
  - Sharing route tables weakens account isolation — harder to demonstrate tenant boundary for HIPAA audits.
  - No built-in service-level visibility per-service (harder to attribute usage to Helios vs Redwood).

When to use: If Helios can host Redwood Private components in the same AWS account (or a dedicated account with explicit peering) and you prefer minimal added components for latency-sensitive internal traffic. Not recommended if strict cross-account tenant isolation is required.

2) AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints + Endpoint Service)- Pros:
  - Strong cross-account isolation. Redwood exposes an endpoint service in our account; Helios creates interface endpoints in theirs — traffic flows over AWS private network via ENIs in Helios VPC.
  - Each endpoint has stable ENI IPs in your subnets which can be allowlisted at your perimeter.
  - Easier to scope audit and billing attribution per endpoint.
  - Works well across accounts and regions (endpoint services can be regional; cross-region requires region-specific endpoints or replication).
- Cons:
  - Slightly higher p95 latency vs peering due to additional ENI hop and endpoint processing — typical delta 2–6ms depending on AZ topology.
  - Throughput per endpoint ENI has limits; for high concurrency we recommend multiple endpoints + load-balanced egress NAT or proxy.

Config notes / recommendations:
  - Place PrivateLink ENIs in dedicated subnets in Helios VPC, behind Helios-managed NAT/proxy for stable egress IPs.
  - Use endpoint policies to restrict which API actions are permitted.
  - For DR/geo redundancy, deploy endpoints in both regions and use Route53 health checks with failover policies (or Redwood routing policy).

3) Site-to-site VPN (IPSec)- Pros:
  - Good for on-prem connectivity and as an emergency fallback path.
  - Fully controllable from Helios firewalls; can be used for bulk non-latency-sensitive transfer or administrative access.
- Cons:
  - Higher and more variable latency; not ideal for low-latency synchronous inference SLAs.
  - Operational overhead: tunnel monitoring, rekey, and potential MTU/fragmentation issues.

Recommendation for Helios setup (short):
- Primary: PrivateLink (regional) into Helios-managed subnets with dedicated ENIs; Redwood provides endpoint-service and documented endpoint policy + expected steady-state ENI IPs.
- High-availability: Multi-AZ endpoints and at least one endpoint per AZ for throughput; replicate endpoints into us-west-2 for DR.
- Backup/DR: S2S VPN from Helios on-prem DR site to Helios VPCs, used only for DR and administrative tasks; do not route prod inference traffic over VPN unless in failover.
- Peering: Only consider peering if Helios wants to host Redwood stack components in a Helios account and accepts the audit implications.

Operational checklist (for MSA/SoW & network teams):
- Static egress IPs for endpoint subnets (list of IPs + change notification SLA).
- CloudTrail + VPC Flow logs delivery to Helios SIEM bucket (retention window: 12 months recommended for audits).
- Endpoint ENI placement, security group rules, and recommended ACLs documented.
- Performance SLO: expected p95 delta vs intra-VPC traffic, agreed throttling/connection limits per endpoint.

I'll prepare a one-page diagram and the endpoint configuration snippets for the call.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Anna / Greg — great to have Greg on the thread. Quick follow-up and proposed next steps so we leave the call with an actionable list: 

Mutual action plan (MAP) — high level items and owners:
1) Redwood: provide PrivateLink endpoint service details, expected ENI IP list (initial + change window) and endpoint policy template — due 2026-11-06. (Owner: David).
2) Helios: confirm subnets and AZs where endpoints will be created and provide firewall allowlist contact — due 2026-11-09. (Owner: Anna / Network Ops).
3) Redwood Security: complete SOC2 control evidence for network-related questions and deliver to Helios S3 bucket (access grant) — due 2026-11-10. (Owner: Security team / Marissa).
4) Both: schedule an on-site or recorded runbook review for incident failover (PrivateLink <-> VPN) and a DR exercise window — target week of 2026-11-22.

Procurement note: static egress IPs are supported via dedicated NAT/proxy placements in your subnets or via a managed egress pool depending on the architecture you select. Dedicated capacity is not strictly required to get stable ENI IPs, but if you want SLA-backed throughput guarantees we can scope a Dedicated capacity block in the SoW. We'll include both options in the MAP.

Calendar: I will send a 30-min invite for Tue 11/3 10:00 PT and attach the one-page decision diagram. After the call we'll update the MAP doc at: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/helios/HL-2026-042 (Doc: mutual-action-plan-hel-042.docx).

If that looks good I'll also open a private Jira: INF-HE-042 for tracking network deliverables and post the technical snippets there.
